title: Airport Runway Taxiway Scheduling Simulation
prompt:
Create a single HTML file with an interactive 3D airport runway and taxiway scheduling simulation using Three.js and GLTFLoader.

## Scene Setup
- Use a perspective camera at position (0, 300, 400) looking at the origin.
- Add ambient light (intensity 0.5) and a directional light from (200, 400, 200) with intensity 0.8 and shadow mapping enabled.
- Renderer should fill the viewport with a dark sky-blue background (0x1a2a3a). Enable shadows on the renderer.
- Create a large flat ground plane (2000x2000) with a dark green material (0x2a5a2a) representing grass.

## Runway & Taxiway Layout
- Create a main runway: a long box (length 800, width 40, height 0.5) centered at origin, oriented along the X-axis, colored dark gray (0x333333) with white dashed center-line markings.
- Create two parallel taxiways: Taxiway Alpha at z = -80 and Taxiway Bravo at z = +80, each 600 units long, 20 units wide, lighter gray (0x555555).
- Create three connector taxiways perpendicular to the runway at x = -200, x = 0, x = +200, connecting the main runway to both taxiways. Each connector is 20 wide, extends from z=-80 to z=+80.
- Place small colored marker lights (emissive spheres, radius 1.5) at each intersection point (6 total on each taxiway). Green = clear, Red = hold. These lights change based on scheduling state.

## Aircraft
- Load the model 'PrimaryIonDrive.glb' using GLTFLoader. This represents a futuristic aircraft/shuttle. Scale it to fit roughly 20 units in length. Clone it to create exactly 4 aircraft instances.
- Aircraft start at these positions:
  - Aircraft 0 (callsign 'ION-01'): x=-350, z=-80 (Taxiway Alpha, west end) heading east
  - Aircraft 1 (callsign 'ION-02'): x=350, z=80 (Taxiway Bravo, east end) heading west
  - Aircraft 2 (callsign 'ION-03'): x=-350, z=80 (Taxiway Bravo, west end) heading east
  - Aircraft 3 (callsign 'ION-04'): x=350, z=-80 (Taxiway Alpha, east end) heading west
- Each aircraft has properties: callsign, currentSegment ('taxiway_alpha'|'taxiway_bravo'|'connector_W'|'connector_C'|'connector_E'|'runway'), status ('idle'|'taxiing'|'holding'|'takeoff_roll'|'departed'), speed (0-60 units/sec), heading (radians).

## Scheduling & Conflict Resolution
- The simulation uses a time-step system. The simulation clock starts at 0.0 seconds and increments in real-time when running.
- Implement a scheduling queue: aircraft request runway access. Only ONE aircraft may occupy the runway at a time. Others must hold at intersection lights (which turn red).
- When an aircraft reaches a connector-runway intersection and the runway is occupied, it stops and its status becomes 'holding'. The intersection light turns red.
- When the runway is clear, the next aircraft in the FIFO queue is granted access, its intersection light turns green, and it proceeds.
- Aircraft performing takeoff_roll accelerate from 0 to 60 units/sec over 3 seconds, then after traveling 400 units on the runway, status becomes 'departed' and the mesh is removed from the scene.
- Maintain a totalDepartures counter and a conflictCount (incremented if two aircraft are ever on the runway simultaneously — this should always be 0 in correct operation).

## User Interactions
- Click on an aircraft (raycasting) to select it. The selected aircraft gets a yellow highlight ring around it. Store selectedAircraftIndex in state.
- Press 'G' to issue 'go' command to the selected aircraft: if idle, it begins taxiing toward the nearest connector to reach the runway. If holding at an intersection and cleared, it proceeds onto the runway for takeoff.
- Press 'H' to force-hold the selected aircraft (override to holding status regardless of clearance).
- Press 'U' to undo the last command issued (restore the aircraft to its previous status and position). Maintain an undo stack of the last 5 commands.
- Press 'R' to redo the last undone command.
- Press 'Space' to pause/resume the simulation clock.
- A DOM button '#btn-auto-schedule' runs the automatic FIFO scheduler for all idle aircraft.
- A DOM button '#btn-reset' resets the entire simulation to initial state.

## HUD / UI
- Top-left HUD panel (DOM overlay, id='hud-panel') showing:
  - Simulation time (id='hud-time')
  - Number of aircraft active (id='hud-active')
  - Total departures (id='hud-departures')
  - Conflict count (id='hud-conflicts')
  - Runway status: 'CLEAR' or callsign of occupant (id='hud-runway-status')
- Bottom panel with the two buttons: '#btn-auto-schedule' and '#btn-reset'.
- When an aircraft is selected, show its callsign and status in a small info box (id='aircraft-info').

## State Management
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with these fields updated every frame:
- simulationTime: number (seconds, 2 decimal precision)
- isPaused: boolean
- aircraftStates: array of 4 objects each with {callsign, status, position: {x, y, z}, speed, heading, currentSegment}
- selectedAircraftIndex: number or null
- runwayOccupant: string (callsign) or null
- totalDepartures: number
- conflictCount: number (must always be 0)
- schedulingQueue: array of callsign strings
- intersectionLights: object mapping intersection names to 'green'|'red'
- undoStackSize: number
- redoStackSize: number
- lastCommand: {type: string, aircraftIndex: number, previousStatus: string} or null
- totalAircraftInScene: number (count of non-departed aircraft meshes)
- groundTruthPositions: array of 4 {x, z} representing expected positions at current time
physics_constraints: Only one aircraft may occupy the runway at any time (conflictCount must remain 0). Aircraft takeoff acceleration is linear: 0 to 60 units/sec over 3 seconds (20 units/sec²). Aircraft depart after 400 units of runway travel. Taxi speed is constant 30 units/sec. All positions must remain within bounds: x in [-500, 500], z in [-150, 150]. Conservation: totalDepartures + totalAircraftInScene must always equal 4. Undo must perfectly restore previous position and status.
